MINUTES
  ADJOURNED PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  MAY 21, 2018

An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order at 6:00 p.m. at the George F Canyon Nature Center, 27305 Palos Verdes Drive East, Rolling
Hills Estates, California by CHAIR ROMANELLI.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIR ROMANELLI led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance

3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Chair Romanelli, Giglia, Persichina, Pope, Wroan, Retz
  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  Portugal
  STAFF PRESENT:  Andy Clark, Community Services Director
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES OF APRIL 16, 2018
  VICE CHAIR GIGLIA moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE
  TO APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF APRIL 16,
  2018
  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so moved.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  A.  STREET TREE REMOVAL APPLICATION

  Community Services Director Clark provided the Park and Activities Commission with a summary
  of the staff report and provided the commission with a copy of an e-mail from Dave Brunnemeyer,
  HOA President, who provided suggestions for the location of the new trees as well as a request to
  provide additional trees.

  Terry Glover, Applicant stated that he is in agreement with staff’s recommendation.

  The Park and Activities Commission held a brief discussion on this item.

  VICE CHAIR GIGLIA, seconded by COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA to,

  APPROVE THE REMOVAL OF TWO EUCALYPTUS STREET TREES LOCATED IN THE
  CIRCULAR DRIVEWAY PLANTER AT 21 MONTECILLO DRIVE AND THE PURCHASE
  OF TWO 15-GALLON TREES TO BE PLANTED IN A LOCATION(S) DETERMINED BY
  THE RESIDENT OR CITY, FOLLOWING THE COMPLETION OF THE HOMEOWNERS
  ASSOCIATION STREET SURVEY, AT THE COST OF THE APPLICANT.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI SO ORDERED.

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS
  A.  QUARTERLY NATURE CENTER REPORT
  Connie Smith, Education Director, Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy (PVPLC) provided
  the Park and Activities Commission with a summary of the nature center’s quarterly report. Also
  present - Adrienne Mohan, Conservation Director, PVPLC.

  A discussion ensued regarding improvements with security, aesthetic improvements to the center,
  planning of more activities, and more promotion of events to surrounding schools and through
  social media.
   In response to a question by CHAIR ROMANELLI, Ms. Smith stated that there are reports that are
  still pending, however, data is still being tracked and stated that it will be prepared for the next
  quarter.

  A discussion ensued regarding tracking the number of hikers who visit the trails as well as
  suggestions on how to use social media to draw attention to the center.

  VICE CHAIR GIGLIA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER RETZ to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE THE QUARTERLY NATURE CENTER REPORT.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

  B.  PROPOSED NEW PARK EQUIPMENT RENTAL FEES

  Community Services Director Clark provided the Park and Activities Commission with a summary
  of the staff report.

  The Park and Activities Commission held a brief discussion on this item.

  VICE CHAIR GIGLIA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER RETZ to,

  MAKE A RECOMMENDATION TO THE CITY COUNCIL TO ADOPT THE FOLLOWING
  EQUIPMENT RENTAL FEES: 1. 10’X10’ CANOPY BOOTH - $75/CANOPY PER DAY; 2.
  4’X4’ CARPETED RISER - $10/RISER PER DAY.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK REPORTS

  COMMISSIONER RETZ stated that some of the rails on PVDE (going towards Narbonne) are
  coming apart.

  B.  CITY CELEBRATION / MUSIC FESTIVAL SUBCOMMITTEE UPDATE

  CHAIR ROMANELLI stated that the subcommittee met with Betty’s Foundation and discussed
  changes to the event including beginning at later time. A decision was made to hold the City
  Celebration and the equestrian event separately. Community Services Director Clark stated that
  the music festival will have a more country music theme.

  9.  DIRECTOR’S ITEMS (Verbal Reports)

  A.  PV STREET FAIR & MUSIC FESTIVAL BOOTH SIGN-UP

  Community Services Director Clark provided the Park and Activities Commission with a sign-up
  sheet for the PV Street Fair and Music Festival booth.

  B.  ROMANIAN FESTIVAL INVITATION

  Community Services Director Clark stated that the Park and Activities Commissioners have been
  invited to attend the Romanian Festival, which will be held on May 26-27, 2018.

  10.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF APRIL 24, 2018

  B.  PLANNING COMMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES OF MAY 7, 2018

  C.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE DRAFT MINUTES OF APRIL 23, 2018

  COMMISSIONER RETZ made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR GIGLIA,

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE ITEMS 10-A THROUGH 10-C

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

Park and Activities Commission  Page 2 of 3
Minutes, May 21, 2018
   11.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  COMMISSIONER ROLES DURING CITYWIDE DISASTERS

  Community Services Director Clark stated that Jessica Slawson, Administrative Analyst will be
  preparing a presentation to bring to the Park and Activities Commission in the near future.

  B.  TEMPORARY STREET BANNERS

  Administrative Assistant Corea suggested installing 4’x8’ boards in the locations designated for
  temporary banner reservations to make installation of banners easier.

  Community Services Clark stated that these items will be added to a future agenda.

  THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION TOURED THE GEORGE F. CANYON NATURE CENTER.

  Connie Smith, Education Director, PVPLC, provided a guided tour of the nature center.

  THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION TOURED DAPPLEGRAY PARK.

  The following items are in need of replacement or repair:

  •  The pedestrian signal at the intersection of PVDN and PVDE may not be ADA compliant.
  •  Dry rot/termites damage on the entry sign to Dapplegray Park.
  •  Books needed for Little Library.
  •  Bottom rail loose on the 3-rail fence across from Dapplegray Park along PVDE.
  •  Dead tree at Dapplegray Park visible from trail along PVDE.
  •  The cap on the 3-rail fence post along the trail on PVDE.

  THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION TOURED THE NEW POCKET PARK ON PALOS
  VERDES DRIVE EAST AND HIGHRIDGE.

  The following items are in need of replacement or repair:

  •  The cap on the 3-rail fence post along PVDE (park street side).

  Community Services Clark stated that the Park and Activities Commission have been asked to discuss a
  name for the park. “John Taber Park” was proposed. No further action was taken.

  It was decided that the pocket park will be reviewed in two phases. In phase 1, the focus will be on the
  lower portion of the park, and in Phase 2, the focus will be on the north side of the park after the
  encroachment issue has been resolved.

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR GIGLIA to,

  ADJOURN THE MEETING AT 7:45 P.M. TO AN ADJOURNED MEETING OF THE PARK
  AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ON JUNE 18, 2018 AT 6:00 P.M. AT ERNIE
  HOWLETT PARK.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

  The next Park and Activities Meeting will be held on Monday, June 18, 2018 at 6:00 p.m. at Ernie
  Howlett Park.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  Carol Corea  Heidi Luce
  Administrative Assistant  City Clerk
